# Cover Letter

[Your address]
[Date]

Dear [Hiring Manager/Recruitment Team],

I am writing to apply for the Community Engagement Officer position at Riverbank Libraries Trust. As someone who has spent the past five years designing and delivering community programmes across the Exeter area, I am genuinely excited by this opportunity to bring energy and partnership-focused approach to your eleven branches.

My volunteer coordination role at Exmouth Food Bank has equipped me with precisely the skills this role demands. I currently recruit, train and support a team of sixty volunteers across four distribution centres—exceeding the scale you are seeking—and I take responsibility for induction, safeguarding training, and retention strategies. This experience has taught me how to build a culture where volunteers feel valued and supported, which I understand is fundamental to your community library model.

Before joining the food bank, I spent two years as an Events Assistant at an independent theatre in Exeter, where I helped develop a schools outreach programme and coordinated monthly community open days. These roles taught me how to design activities for diverse audiences and how to build partnerships that genuinely embed an organisation within its community. What matters to me most is reaching people who don't currently engage with cultural or community services—and this is precisely where libraries excel.

I have managed an annual budget of £12,000 for volunteer expenses and training, and whilst this is smaller than your £48,000 programme budget, it has required the same discipline in allocation, reporting and demonstrating value for money. I produce monthly reports for our trustees covering participation, volunteer retention and impact, and I contributed significantly to a successful £25,000 National Lottery Community Fund application by compiling participation data and case studies. I am confident I can scale these skills to manage your programme budget and quarterly board reporting.

Growing up and still living in Exeter, I have deep knowledge of the area and its communities. Through my work, I have already built relationships with two of the primary schools mentioned on your website, and I understand many of the local voluntary sector partners you work with. However, it is my genuine commitment to access and inclusion—not just local knowledge—that draws me to this role. I believe libraries are uniquely positioned to reach people marginalised by other services, and I am committed to making that happen.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in volunteer leadership, community partnerships, and programme delivery can help Riverbank Libraries Trust deepen its reach across Exeter.

Yours faithfully,

[Your name]
